title: Token Workbench: interactive cost breakdown, attribution & export patterns
creator: Elena Park
description: Create a unified "Token Workbench" UX pattern that lets engineers and finance users explore token-level costs across dimensions (model, route, client, time), perform attribution, and export canonical reports. Deliver high-fidelity prototypes, a small component library spec, and recommended pricing UI patterns for volumetric/tiered previews and per-route overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive workbench allows filtering by model, route, timeframe, and client ID and updates cost breakdown in <1s for typical dataset samples
Attribution view supports top-N contributing prompts and percentage allocation with configurable attribution heuristics (prefix, KV-cache hits, streaming overhead)
Export supports CSV and parquet schemas with clear column mapping and includes a pricing-preview flag in exports
Design tokens and components documented in Figma file and linked to component library (tokens + variants)
Prototype usability test (n=6 engineers, 3 finance users) completed with identified usability issues logged
prototype_notes: Primary canvas shows cost waterfall: total tokens -> generation tokens -> KV cache saves -> per-route markup -> unit pricing -> net cost
Cross-filtering: clicking a model row drills into per-route token distribution and exposes sample prompts that contributed most tokens (with redaction toggle)
Attribution modes: naive (token count), weighted (generation vs system prompt), and backend-adjusted (applies realized latency overhead)
Pricing preview: overlay that lets you toggle pricing rules (volume tiers, reserved discounts, per-route custom prices) and see projected invoice impact
Export options: 'Operational' (token granularity) vs 'Accounting' (monthly rolled-up with pricing applied)
decisions: Keep attribution heuristics configurable but default to weighted (70% generation, 30% system/prefix) to better reflect billed work
Export schema will include both raw token counts and 'priced_token_units' to allow downstream reconciliation without needing internal price tables
Design will favor a single workbench canvas (filters + breakdown + preview) rather than separate screens to reduce context switches
tradeoffs: Performance vs fidelity: showing sample prompts increases clarity but may expose PII; implemented redaction and sampling to mitigate and keep UI performant
Complexity vs discoverability: exposing pricing rules inline adds cognitive load for new users; introduced a simplified 'preview' mode and an 'advanced pricing' accordion
Consistency vs innovation: reuse existing console chart components for speed of implementation, but extend them with micro-interactions that require small runtime changes
